title: Ordinal Number Worksheets for Kindergarten — First to Eighth
intro: Distinguish an object's position from the number of objects.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Establish that counting begins at the left. Point to each position in order, then have the student select just the requested object.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Touch the leftmost animal and say “first.” Move to the next and say “second,” then to the next and say “third.” Leave a finger on that one animal. It is the third animal even though six animals are in the whole line.

On this worksheet, “Circle the third picture” means draw one circle around the picture in position 3. It does not mean circle any three pictures.

Ask your student

Does third mean three objects or one object in a certain place?

If your student needs help

If several objects are circled, count positions together and stop on the requested one.
